data.name: Vidyutvan
data.gender_notes: Vidyutvan is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Vidyutvan is a name derived from the Sanskrit word 'Vidyut', which means lightning, and 'Van', which means forest or protector. The name Vidyutvan carries the meaning “God of Lightning” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit, Hindi, etc. tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Vidyutvan usually hope their child will grow to embody god of lightning and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Represents divine power and swiftness, a guardian of light.
data.etymology: Vidyutvan belongs to the Sanskrit, Hindi, etc. linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “God of Lightning.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Vidyutvan total 3, giving a life-path number of 3. Number 3 is linked with Jupiter and with the qualities of creativity, expression and optimism.

The name Vidyutvan evokes images of power, energy, and the raw, untamed wonders of nature.

It represents protection, strength, and the power to overcome any obstacles that come one's way. The name can inspire one to live a fierce, powerful, and determined life, overcoming challenges and pursuing their goals with unwavering focus and resilience.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Vidyutvan symbolizes the radiant and electrifying wisdom that illuminates the path to enlightenment. The name signifies the dynamic force of knowledge, transcending the ordinary and igniting the soul with the spark of divine understanding.

historical_references.reference: Vidyutvan was a celebrated Jain monk and scholar who lived during the 12th century in India. He is best known for his work 'Agama Prakasha' which is a commentary on the Jain Agamas.

Another reference suggests that Vidyutvan was a powerful Jain Tirthankara (ford-maker) who lived before the Mahavira's time in the 8th or 9th century. This reference is found in the 'Kalpa Sutra' of Acharya Hemchandrasuriswami.
